audit.question: Why 3.5 T?
audit.answer: 1.6 set mu0 Ms to the highest polarization any known material reaches: about 3.5 T, the 4f moments of Dy and Ho (about 10 Bohr magnetons per atom at their density, measured only near 4 K). Fe65Co35 (2.45 T) is the room-temperature record; the canon temperature shape was kept and only its magnitude was capped.

audit.question: Screening limit or fundamental limit?
audit.answer: A screening limit. Nothing fundamental stops more moment per atom: an atom with all d spins aligned gives 5 Bohr magnetons (about 5 T at iron density), and aligning every electron would give about 26 T, which Pauli pairing of the core shells forbids. 3.5 T is the edge of established materials, not of physics.

audit.question: What does the amplification law define?
audit.answer: Fiji 05_LATTICE_LAW defines A_B(T) as a smoothstep from 1 below 650 K to 30 at 1100 K (26.34 at 1000 K) and B_eff = B_seed A_B. 1.6 read A_B as the ratio Ms(T)/Ms(cold), a material property; read as a field gain it has no geometry, no volume and no energy source, so it is not a field law (section C).

audit.question: Did the geometry constrain the result?
audit.answer: Yes, mostly. The 0.2 m liners sit 2-8 m from the burn; their geometry factor is G = 2.95e-03, so even the canon field would need mu0 Ms = 50271 T there. A 2-30 m shell (G = 4.7) still needed 35 T. The volume close to the burn, not the material, sets the field.

audit.question: Is the orientation realizable?
audit.answer: Not with the 1.6 constitutive law alone. 1.6 used the optimal dipole orientation at every point (times a texture and a 16-segment factor) but magnetized the material with tanh(B_seed/B_align), i.e. a seeded, field-following material. A fixed orientation against the local field needs a coercivity (anisotropy field) the brief does not grant. 1.6A computes both: SEEDED (M along the local H, one property) and ORIENTED (a fixed easy axis, with the coercivity it would need).

audit.question: Were demagnetizing fields, mutual interactions and mechanical loads included?
audit.answer: Partly. 1.6 integrated the dipole kernel for the field at a target outside the material (exact there) and the force from the coil-field gradient, but no demagnetizing field, no liner-to-liner interaction, no self-consistent M, and no flux conservation in the coils on collapse. 1.6A adds all four.

audit.question: What changes outside the range of known materials?
audit.answer: Field, energy and force scale with mu0 Ms (linearly at fixed geometry, forces and self-energy with its square). Above about 2.5 T the moment per atom passes the Slater-Pauling maximum of metallic alloys; above about 5 T it passes a full d shell at iron density; 10 T needs rare-earth moments at transition-metal density. At 1000 K no known hard magnet keeps coercivity (Nd2Fe14B, FePt and SmCo5 lose their order at about 590, 750 and 1020 K).

audit.question: Which assumptions dominate the conclusions?
audit.answer: In order: (1) the Fiji volume and its distance from the burn (field falls as distance cubed); (2) the 1.5 photon power, which makes every surface in line of sight thermally infeasible whatever its material; (3) the fast-neutron fluence limit of REBCO; (4) mu0 Ms; (5) whether a fixed orientation is allowed. The radiator ratio is set by (2), not by Fiji.

solver.chosen: an axisymmetric bound-current integral solver in the standard library (uniform-M ring cells -> surface currents -> Gauss-Legendre loops with exact elliptic-integral fields). For linear-recoil and seeded (tanh) materials in free space it is the integral form of what Magpylib or RADIA compute; it is validated below against closed forms. Nonlinear B-H curves inside soft iron, eddy currents and 3D (non-axisymmetric) segmentation are outside it.

successor.law: B_total(r, T) = B_coils(r) + B_Fiji(r; M(r, T)),  M = Ms_max f(T) g(H) along the local H (SEEDED) or the easy axis (ORIENTED, needs coercivity),  f(T) = the canon smoothstep from 1/A_max (activation) to 1 (saturation), linear to 0 from degradation to quench, x (1 - cycle loss)^n, collapse above the strain limit; dM/dt = (M_eq - M)/tau
successor.A_sys: A_sys(T) = B_total(burn, T) / B_coils(burn) = 1 + (B_Fiji(burn; Ms_max) / B_coils(burn)) f(T)/f(T_op): saturates at 1 + B_Fiji/B_coils, never at A_max; it is computed from geometry and Ms, not assumed
